tools.name: upload_asset
tools.description:
Upload a reference image, start frame, video or audio file and get an asset id to pass as
`inputs` ({slot: [asset ids]}; slot names come from list_capabilities). Give exactly one of: `path` (a local file; only when the server runs locally over stdio),

tools.name: generate
tools.description:
Run a capability (see list_capabilities). `model` is optional; the capability's first available model,
in list_capabilities order, is used. estimate_cost shows which model that is and its price.
`inputs` maps slot names to asset ids, e.g. {"images": [id1, id2]} for image.edit or
{"start_frame": [id]

tools.name: get_job
tools.description:
Current status of a generation job: queued, in_progress, completed, failed, nsfw or canceled.

as shortcuts), plus credits estimated and actually charged. `job_id` is the `request_id` returned by

tools.name: wait_for_job
tools.description:
Wait for a job to finish, polling for up to timeout_s seconds (max 600). Returns the final status,
or the latest status with a note if it is still running; call again to keep waiting. `job_id` is the
`request_id` returned by generate.

tools.description:
Get a generated (or uploaded) file. `asset` is an asset id or the asset url from a job status.
Locally (stdio) the file is saved to `path` (default: current directory, named after the asset id)
and the saved path is returned. Remotely (HTTP) nothing is saved: a short-lived signed download URL is
ret

tools.name: cancel_job
tools.description:
Cancel a job that has not finished. A model call already running is not interrupted, but its result
is discarded. Returns the job's status afterwards. `job_id` is the `request_id` returned by generate.

tools.name: list_recent_jobs
tools.description:
Most recent generation jobs in one project, newest first (limit 1-200), with status, outputs and
credits. The project is `project` if given, else the API key's default; jobs in other projects are not
included, so to see everything call list_projects and pass each. Filter by `workflow_run_id` to see

tools.name: list_assets
tools.description:
Assets in a project, newest first: uploads and generated outputs, with kind, size, dimensions and the
job that produced them. Use their ids as inputs to generate.

tools.name: get_balance
tools.description:
The organization's credits: `available` (spendable now), `held` (reserved by running jobs, already
excluded from available), totals `by_source` (plan, top-up, grant), the next expiry, and each credit lot.
Jobs are refused when available credits are below their estimate; top-ups happen in the dashboa

tools.name: list_projects
tools.description:
Projects in the caller's organization. Every asset and job belongs to one; when a tool's `project` is
omitted the API key's default project (or the organization's default) is used. `project` accepts a project
id or slug. Set archived=true to include archived projects alongside active ones.

tools.name: create_project
tools.description:
Create a project to keep a piece of work's assets and jobs together. Returns it with its id and slug.

`kind` says what the project is for (general, film, game, ads, app; default general). It picks the project's icon and
which presets, workflows and docs are shown first, and never restricts what the

tools.name: update_project
tools.description:
Change a project's name, slug, description or kind (general, film, game, ads, app). `project` is its id or slug.
Only the fields given are changed; an empty `description` clears it. Returns the updated project.

tools.name: list_items
tools.description:

style, sequence or set. Each has `id`, `slug`, `name`, `kind` and `starred_take_id`. Filter by `kind`.
`project` is its id or slug. Items are addressed by id, slug or `@slug` (the form used in pr

tools.name: get_item
tools.description: One item of a project. `item` is its id, slug or `@slug`.

tools.name: create_item
tools.description:
Create an item in a project. `kind` is character, place, object, style, sequence or set. The `slug`
(default: derived from `name`) is unique in the project and is how prompts and tools refer to it, as `@slug`.
`parent_item_id` makes the item a shot of a sequence item. Pass the item to generate or ru

star_take

`take_id` comes from list_takes. Returns the take.

directory over stdio, or a short-lived signed URL over HTTP), tagged with `item` and `take_id`. Give `item`
(id, slug or `@slug`) for one item, else every item in the project is covered. Give `take

tools.name: list_workflows
tools.description:
Ready-made workflows (e.g. text-to-clip, product-to-ad, effect presets): multi-step pipelines built on the
capabilities. Each has an `inputs` form (name -> type, label, required, default, options for choices),
its `outputs`, the steps it runs, `available` with `unavailable_reasons`, and `credits_est

tools.name: get_workflow
tools.description: One workflow by slug, with its input form, outputs, steps, availability and credit estimate.

tools.name: estimate_workflow
tools.description:
Credits a workflow run would cost with these inputs, without running it. Validates the inputs against
the workflow's form. Media inputs take one asset id from upload_asset or an earlier job, a public https URL
or a data: URI. Also returns
`available_credits`, the organization's spendable balance.

tools.name: run_workflow
tools.description:
Run a workflow. `inputs` fills its form (see list_workflows): text and choice values as strings, media
as one asset id, public https URL or data: URI each. Credits are the sum of its steps; the run reports estimate and actual. With
wait=false (default) it returns the queued run with its id; with wai

tools.name: get_run
tools.description:
A workflow run: status (queued, running, completed, failed, canceled), each step's status, generation
request and outputs, the run's named `outputs`, and credits. wait=true polls up to timeout_s (max 600).

tools.name: list_runs
tools.description: Recent workflow runs, newest first (limit 1-200), optionally for one workflow slug.

tools.name: cancel_run
tools.description: Cancel an unfinished workflow run; its pending and running steps and their generation jobs are canceled.

findings.title: Anomalously long tool description
findings.detail: Description of "generate" is 1777 chars, far longer than this server's median (307). Overlong descriptions are a common place to bury instructions.

findings.title: Lethal trifecta: untrusted input + private data + external sink
findings.detail: Server "mcp" exposes tools that together enable an exfiltration flow. Untrusted content: upload_asset, generate, get_job, download_asset, list_takes, export · Private data: upload_asset, generate, download_asset, list_recent_jobs, list_projects, create_item, export, run_workflow · Public sink: upload_asset, generate · Destructive: list_capabilities, estimate_cost, upload_asset, generate, download_asset, list_recent_jobs, create_project, estimate_workflow, run_workflow, get_run, cancel_run.

evidence.snippet: Untrusted content: upload_asset, generate, get_job, download_asset, list_takes, export · Private data: upload_asset, generate, download_asset, list_recent_jobs, list_projects, create_item, export, run_workflow · Public sink: upload_asset, generate · Destructive: list_capabilities, estimate_cost, upload_asset, generate, download_asset, list_recent_jobs, create_project, estimate_workflow, run_workflow, get_run, cancel_run

findings.remediation: Do not co-install these capabilities under one trust boundary; an injected comment/email can steer the model to exfiltrate via the sink tool.
